events.text: You have stood on the Spire and been everything a soul can be: beggar, emperor, beast, a god of your own small world. This time you will be none of it. Far below, in a house you could cover with a thumb, someone has just been born. The midwife says the name aloud: {name}. You will not live this life. You will only watch it.

choices.text: Lean over the edge of heaven and look closely

effects.log: The baby yawns. Something in you that climbed a hundred floors sits down to see what happens next.

choices.text: Fold your hands, and let the world turn on its own

effects.log: Whatever this life is, it belongs to {name}. You set your power down beside you, where it can wait.

events.text: Again the long look down, and again a newborn: {name}, red-faced and furious at the cold. You remember the last life you watched, every year of it, the times you reached down and the times you did not. You know now how fast a mortal life goes by from up here. Like a lamp carried past a window.

choices.text: Promise yourself a lighter hand this time

effects.log: You make the promise to nobody. Heaven does not keep records of a god's promises. You will.

choices.text: Promise yourself nothing at all

effects.log: You will see who {name} becomes, and decide then. That is the only honest promise up here.

events.text: The baby below has nobody. A bundle left on the step of a shrine in the rain, a name pinned to the blanket in a hurried hand: {name}. A temple servant finds it at dawn and grumbles and takes it in. From up here you could have stopped the rain. You notice that you want to, very much, and that you have not yet decided what kind of god you are.

choices.text: Keep the cold off, just for tonight

effects.log: The rain thins to a mist above that one step. The bundle sleeps. Nobody below will ever know why.

choices.text: Let it be as it is, and watch

effects.log: The servant's hands are rough and warm. It turns out the world already had a kindness ready. You did not need to send one.

events.text: A great house below: lanterns on every gate, servants running, an old matriarch weeping with relief at the cradle. The child is {name}, born to more than most mortals will ever own, and already wrapped in the weight of it. From up here the courtyard walls look exactly like the walls of a cage.

choices.text: Wish the child a door in that wall

effects.log: Somewhere in the great house a gardener leaves a gate unlatched, and keeps forgetting to fix it for years.

choices.text: Let the house be the house

effects.log: Walls or no walls, it is the child's life to climb out of or not. You settle in to watch.

events.text: A comet crosses the sky on the night {name} is born, and every fortune-teller in the province has something to say about it. You were there: you watched it go past at arm's length, the way a mortal watches a moth. It means nothing. Below, it will mean whatever they decide it means, and the child will carry that.

choices.text: Let the comet mean something good

effects.log: The loudest fortune-teller in town wakes up with a happy prophecy in mind, and cannot think why.

choices.text: Let them make of it what they will

effects.log: You do not touch the stories. Mortals have always written their own sky.

events.text: {name} is small and fierce now, running the lanes with a stick for a sword, conquering a woodpile, losing to a goose. Every child in the murim plays at being a great master. You have been a great master. It was nothing like this, and also it was exactly like this.

choices.text: Smile, and let the goose win

effects.log: The goose wins. {name} cries, then laughs, then plans revenge on the goose for a week.

choices.text: Wonder what this child will become

effects.log: You try to see the shape of the life ahead. You cannot. It has not happened yet. That is the point of it.

events.text: Night in a small house. {name} sleeps between two grown-ups who are arguing in whispers about money, and stop when the child stirs, and go on more softly. You have had parents like these in other lives. You know what a whisper costs.

choices.text: Let the argument end kindly tonight

effects.log: One of them laughs at something the other says, and the argument is over. {name} sleeps on, untroubled.

choices.text: Listen, and do nothing

effects.log: They make it up on their own, the way people do. You file that away: they did not need you.

events.text: {name} is hungry. Not hungry like a child before dinner: hungry the way that changes the shape of a face. There is an orchard wall on the way to nowhere, and a peach tree behind it, and a peach the size of a fist hanging just too high.

choices.text: A small wind

effects.log: The peach falls. {name} looks at it, then up at the sky, then eats it, very fast, before anyone can take it away.

choices.text: Watch the child find a way

effects.log: It takes an hour and a borrowed ladder, and {name} is caught and chased, and eats the peach anyway. You are absurdly proud.

events.text: There is a roadside shrine with no name on it, only moss and a chipped bowl. {name} stops there on the way home, puts a pebble in the bowl because there is nothing else to give, and prays, in a child's whisper, to whoever is listening. Nobody has ever prayed to you before. Not like this. Not to you without a name.

choices.text: Listen to every word

effects.log: It is about a lost kite and a sick dog and a friend who said something cruel. You listen to all of it as if it were a sutra.

choices.text: Answer with a warm wind

effects.log: A warm wind comes down the road out of a cold sky. {name} goes home with a feeling that will be remembered for years.

choices.text: Stay silent: a god who answers pebbles answers everything

effects.log: The bowl keeps the pebble. You keep your power. Some silences are a kind of respect.

events.text: {name} is hurt, badly, lying in the dark somewhere that smells of straw and old blood, and prays the way people pray who do not believe in anything: "If anyone is up there. If anyone at all." You are up here. You have always been up here, this whole life.

choices.text: Answer: let the pain ease before dawn

effects.log: The pain loosens like a fist opening. {name} sleeps at last, and wakes believing in something small.

choices.text: Stay with {p_him} through the night, and only that

effects.log: You do nothing a mortal could see. But {name} is not alone in the dark, and somehow knows it.

choices.text: Stay silent: this is {p_his} to survive

effects.log: Dawn comes. {name} is still alive, by no grace but {p_his} own. That counts for something too.

events.text: {name} kneels at the family altar, not for {p_him}self this time. For the people at the table: that the little ones grow, that the cough in the next room is only a cough. It is the oldest prayer there is. You have prayed it yourself, in lives when you had nobody up here to pray to.

choices.text: Answer: let the cough be only a cough

effects.log: By the new moon the house is quiet at night again. {name} lights an extra stick of incense and does not know for whom.

choices.text: Listen, and remember every name

effects.log: You learn the names of everyone {name} loves. It is a long list. It is longer than you expected.

events.text: {name} has done things this life that do not wash off. Tonight, at a ruined shrine, {p_he} prays, but not for forgiveness: for power, more power, enough that nobody can ever touch {p_him} again. The prayer is ugly and honest. It is the most honest thing {name} has said in years.

choices.text: Answer: not with power

effects.log: You send no power. You send a memory instead: a peach, a goose, a stick for a sword. {name} sits in the ruin for a long time.

choices.text: Stay silent: you will not feed this

effects.log: The shrine stays dark. {name} curses whoever is not listening, and goes, and the curse is one more thing you carry.

events.text: {name} is old enough now to pray without asking for anything. On a quiet evening {p_he} burns one stick of incense at the nameless shrine on the hill and says only: "Thank you. Whoever you are. For all of it." You did not do all of it. You did not even do most of it.

choices.text: Accept the thanks

effects.log: You take it as it is given, the way a mortal takes a cup of tea. It is warm. It is enough.

choices.text: Answer: the incense burns all night

effects.log: The one stick burns until dawn and never seems to shorten. In the morning {name} laughs out loud, alone on the hill.

events.text: Before the hardest day of {p_his} life so far, {name} cannot sleep, and walks out under the stars, and asks them for luck. The stars cannot hear. You can. You have heard this exact prayer from a thousand mouths, in a thousand lives, and some of them were yours.

choices.text: Answer: one clear night's sleep

effects.log: {name} goes back in and sleeps like a stone, and wakes clear-headed and early.

choices.text: Listen, and let tomorrow be what it is

effects.log: Tomorrow comes. Whatever happens in it, {name} faced it on {p_his} own two feet.

choices.text: Stay silent

effects.log: The stars do what stars do. You keep your hand still.

events.text: In the middle of a crowded market road {name} stops, so suddenly that a porter walks into {p_him}, and looks straight up. Not at the sky. At you. There is no way a mortal can see this far. {name} is looking anyway, frowning, like someone who has heard their name called in an empty house.

choices.text: Let {p_him} feel you there

effects.log: For one breath {name} knows, beyond doubt, that someone is watching, and that they mean no harm. It never leaves {p_him}.

choices.text: Draw back behind the clouds

effects.log: The feeling fades. {name} shakes it off, apologises to the porter, and buys the wrong vegetables.

events.text: Over cheap wine, {name} tells a friend something {p_he} has never told anyone: "Sometimes I think someone watches over me. Not my ancestors. Someone else. Someone who does not know what to do with me either." The friend laughs. {name} does not.

choices.text: Let the next cup taste of plum blossom

effects.log: It is ordinary wine, and it tastes of spring. {name} goes very still, and then smiles into the cup.

choices.text: Say nothing; it is a secret worth keeping

effects.log: You leave the wine as it is. Some things are better half believed.

events.text: {name} stands on a hill in the wind and shouts at the sky: "Whoever you are, stop helping me! I did not ask for you! If I rise, I want it to be mine!" A flock of crows goes up at the noise. You are, you realise, being told off by your own mortal.

choices.text: Step back, as asked

effects.log: You fold your hands. From now on, whatever {name} wins will be {p_his} own. It is the most respectful thing you have ever done.

choices.text: Stay close anyway, but quieter

effects.log: You do not leave. You only learn to be more careful. {name} goes home grumbling, oddly comforted.

events.text: Old now, {name} sits on the step in the evening and speaks to the empty air as if to a friend across the yard: "I always knew you were there. I never knew what you were. I hope it was not too boring, watching me." It was not. Not once.

choices.text: Let {p_him} hear one word of yours

effects.log: A single word, in no language, in the wind through the eaves. {name} nods as if it settled an old argument.

choices.text: Answer in the only way a god should: by listening

effects.log: You say nothing and listen to all of it, the whole evening. When {name} goes in, it is with a light step.

events.text: {name} has blood on {p_his} hands, and lately cannot shake a feeling of being seen. Not judged: seen. A cold weight between the shoulder blades, at night, after. {name} starts sleeping with a lamp lit. You did not mean to be a haunting.

choices.text: Let {p_him} feel what you feel: not anger, sorrow

effects.log: One night the weight turns into something else, sadder and gentler. {name} weeps, and does not know why, and is changed a little.

choices.text: Withdraw, and let {p_him} sleep

effects.log: You pull back. The lamp burns down. {name} sleeps at last, and the deeds stay exactly as heavy as they were.

events.text: {name} has broken through: {realm} at last, after years of failing at the gate. You watched every failure from up here, the nosebleeds, the dawns, the quiet giving-up and the starting again. You could have opened the gate at any time. You did not. Now {p_he} is through it, and it is entirely {p_his} own.

choices.text: Hold your hand: let the victory stay whole

effects.log: You do not add a thing. {name} sits in the dawn, shaking, with nothing in {p_his} chest but {p_his} own strength.

choices.text: Steady {p_his} breath, just for a moment

effects.log: The new energy settles like water finding its level. {name} thinks it was luck.

events.text: A wedding below: red lanterns, drums, a crowd of aunts. {name} looks terrified and very happy, which is the right way to look. You could make this marriage lucky. You could make it last. You have seen what a god's hand does to a marriage in the stories. It is never what the god meant.

choices.text: Bless it quietly, no more than a good omen

effects.log: A pair of magpies settle on the roof during the vows. The aunts are delighted. That is all you do.

choices.text: Hold your hand: love has to be built by the ones inside it

effects.log: You leave it to them. They will quarrel and mend and quarrel. It will be theirs.

events.text: {name} holds a newborn for the first time and stares at it with the exact expression you wore, a whole life ago, looking down at {name}. Now there are two lives below you, and you can feel already that one will take your eyes off the other.

choices.text: Watch them both, a little each

effects.log: You learn the trick of it the way every parent does: you never really look away from either.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on {name}; the child will have its own heaven

effects.log: This one is not yours to watch. Somewhere, perhaps, another god leans closer.

events.text: {name} kneels in a sect's courtyard and takes the oath. A new name, a new robe, a master who looks exactly as tired as masters always look. You know this sect: you were in it, or one like it, a dozen lives ago. You know which elder is kind and which one is not.

choices.text: Nudge {p_him} toward the kind elder

effects.log: On the first morning {name} takes a wrong turn and ends up sweeping the kind elder's courtyard. It changes everything, quietly.

choices.text: Let {p_him} find out for {p_him}self

effects.log: It will take {name} a year and one bad lesson to learn what you already know. It will be worth more learned that way.

events.text: A fork in an ordinary road. One way goes to the city, the other goes home, and {name} has stood here long enough that a farmer with a cart has gone round twice. You can see where both roads lead. You can see, for once, very clearly. It would be so easy to tip the balance with a breath of wind.

choices.text: Hold your hand: the not-knowing is the life

effects.log: You do not breathe. {name} chooses, as mortals do, for no reason anyone could write down.

choices.text: A breath of wind toward the better road

effects.log: The wind turns. {name} follows it without knowing why, and the better road is better, for now.

events.text: {name} has a blade at someone's throat, a helpless someone, and is deciding. You can see the whole life on either side of this moment. You could knock the blade aside with a gust. You could also let {name} be what {p_he} chooses to be. There is no version of this where you are not responsible.

choices.text: A gust knocks the blade aside

effects.log: The blade skids across the stones. The helpless one runs. {name} stares at {p_his} empty hand, shaken, and lets it go.

choices.text: Let {p_him} choose, and live with what {p_he} chooses

effects.log: You do nothing. It is the hardest nothing you have ever done. Whatever happens next, it is {name}'s.

events.text: {name} is old now. The hands that held a stick for a sword shake when they pour tea. From up here a mortal life is so short you can see the whole of it at once, like a scroll unrolled on a table: the beginning, the long middle, and the end, not far off now.

choices.text: Sit with {p_him} through one more winter

effects.log: The winter is mild. The tea is good. {name} sits in the sun more than usual, and does not know why it feels like company.

choices.text: Begin, quietly, to say goodbye

effects.log: You start to remember the life instead of watching it. It is a strange thing, to grieve someone who is still pouring tea.

events.text: The house is full of {name}'s people now: children grown, little ones underfoot, someone always cooking. {name} sits at the centre of it, half deaf and entirely content, and you realise the life you have been watching has become a crowd of lives. You cannot follow all of them. You were never meant to.

choices.text: Let one evening be perfect

effects.log: Nobody quarrels, the rice is not burnt, the old one laughs at every joke. They will all remember that evening.

choices.text: Let it be ordinary, which is better

effects.log: Someone burns the rice. Everyone blames the cat. {name} has never been happier, and you did nothing at all.

events.text: {name} grows old alone. Not unhappily, exactly: there is a cat, and a garden, and a neighbour who brings soup on feast days. But the evenings are long, and {p_he} talks to the sky more than {p_he} used to. You are, it turns out, the closest friend {name} has left.

choices.text: Send a visitor down the road

effects.log: An old acquaintance passes through town and knocks, and stays a week. {name} is grumpy about it and glad.

choices.text: Keep {p_him} company the only way you can: by staying

effects.log: You stay. The evenings are long for you too. You find you do not mind them.

events.text: {name} dies in the night, old and in bed, at the end of a long road. There is no last great moment. Just a breath that does not come back, a house that wakes to quiet, someone running for the neighbours. You watched every year of it. You know this life better than {name} did.

choices.text: Close the book gently

effects.log: The book of {name} closes. Up here there is no grave to visit. There is only you, and all of it, remembered.

choices.text: Say {p_his} name once, aloud, in heaven

effects.log: You say it. Heaven is very large and very quiet, and the name goes on and on in it. It will be there long after you have gone back to the wheel.

events.text: It is over quickly, the way it so often is in the murim: a road, a blade, a stranger, a moment nobody saw coming. {name} is gone before you can lean closer. You have died like this yourself, more times than you can count. It is worse from up here. From up here you see everything that will now never happen.

choices.text: Grieve it, all of it

effects.log: You let yourself grieve the long middle that never came, the children never had, the old age never reached. Then you close the book.

choices.text: Remember only what was

effects.log: Not what might have been. What was: the goose, the peach, the first dawn at the gate. It was a whole life. A short one is still whole.

events.text: You pulled {name} back from death once. It bought years: you can count them, each one, a road walked and a meal eaten and a face loved that would not have been. Now death comes again, and this time you let it in, as you always knew you would have to.

choices.text: Count the years you gave

effects.log: You count them. They were good years, most of them. You do not regret one.

choices.text: Wonder whether you should have

effects.log: You will never know whether those years were a gift or a theft from some other fate. A god does not get to know that. Nobody does.

events.text: In the whole of {name}'s life, you never once reached down. Not for the hunger, not for the wounds, not for the long nights of prayer. You watched. And {name} lived every hour of it on {p_his} own strength, and never knew how hard it was for the one watching to keep still.

choices.text: Close the book, and be proud of {p_him}

effects.log: Every step of it was {name}'s. You did not take one. That was the gift.

choices.text: Wonder if {p_he} ever felt alone

effects.log: Perhaps. Perhaps not. You were there the whole time. You will have to trust that something of that got through.

events.text: You reached down so many times: an omen here, a blessing there, a stranger sent down the road. Now {name} is gone, and you sit with the question every meddling god sits with in the end. Whose life was it, really? The mortal's, or yours?

choices.text: Theirs. You only helped.

effects.log: You choose to believe it. Most of it was {name}'s. The parts that were yours, {p_he} made into {p_his} own.

choices.text: Both, and that is not a bad thing

effects.log: A life is never one person's. Every mortal is carried by a hundred hands. Yours were only some of them.

events.text: Another life watched to its end. You are getting better at this, and worse: better at keeping still, worse at the end, because you know now how much a mortal life holds, and how fast it goes, and that the next one you watch will go just as fast. {name} is gone. You will remember {p_him} with the others.

choices.text: Set {p_his} name beside the others

effects.log: There is a quiet place in you where the watched lives are kept. {name} goes there, beside the last. It is not crowded yet.

choices.text: Close the book gently

effects.log: The book of {name} closes. Up here there is no grave to visit. There is only you, and all of it, remembered.

events.text: You choose a sign and set it in {name}'s path. Mortals have read the sky for omens since there were mortals; this time there is really someone writing in it. What do you write?

choices.text: A cracked bowl at breakfast: be careful

effects.log: The bowl splits clean in two in {name}'s hands. All that week {p_he} walks slower, sleeps lighter, and turns down the road through the pass.

choices.text: A white crane over the road: go on, be bold

effects.log: A white crane rises off the paddy just as {name} hesitates at the crossroads, and flies the far way. {name} follows it.

choices.text: A lamp that will not go out: hope

effects.log: The little lamp by {name}'s bed burns all night on no oil at all. In the morning the world seems possible again.

events.text: A sign for {name}, then. Not a thunderbolt: a mortal who sees a thunderbolt runs mad or founds a cult. Something small enough to be doubted and strong enough to be remembered.

choices.text: Three crows on the gate: stay home a while

effects.log: {name} counts them twice, frowns, and decides the journey can wait. The rest of the year passes in safe, dull days.

choices.text: A shooting star at the wrong time of night: reach higher

effects.log: It is the wrong season and the wrong hour for it. {name} watches it fall and starts the hard thing {p_he} had been putting off.

events.text: {name} is old enough now to laugh at omens and still look twice at them. You choose one anyway. The old learn to read the world very closely. They have less of it left.

choices.text: Plum blossom in winter: be gentle with yourself

effects.log: One branch flowers in the snow outside the window. {name} takes the hint, and rests, for once.

choices.text: A sword that sings on the wall: one more road

effects.log: The old sword hums in the night. {name} takes it down at dawn and goes out to see what is still out there.

events.text: You send {name} a dream. Mortals dream every night and forget by breakfast; a god's dream is the one that stays. You can shape it any way you like. You think about what this life needs, and what {name} would want, which is not always the same.

choices.text: A dream of a mountain path climbing into the clouds

effects.log: {name} wakes before dawn, aching to train, and does not stop for years. Something above is calling.

choices.text: A dream of a face {p_he} has not yet met

effects.log: {name} wakes with a face in mind and a feeling of being late for someone. Every crowd, now, {p_he} searches.

choices.text: A dream of someone {p_he} could have helped

effects.log: {name} wakes ashamed of nothing in particular, and that day gives a beggar a whole meal. It becomes a habit.

choices.text: A dream of home, warm and plain

effects.log: {name} wakes homesick for a place that might not exist, and spends the next years building one.

events.text: Night again, and {name} asleep, and the long dark of a sleeping mind open to you like a door. The last dream you sent is still in there somewhere, worn smooth with remembering. What do you add?

choices.text: A dream of an old master who nods once

effects.log: {name} wakes certain {p_he} is on the right road, and walks it harder.

choices.text: A dream of a hand held in the dark

effects.log: {name} wakes lonely in a new way, and starts to say yes to invitations.

choices.text: A dream of a field after rain

effects.log: {name} wakes calm, and stops picking fights that do not need picking.

events.text: A child's dream, then, for a child's head: {name} is small enough that dreams and days still run together. Be careful. What you send now will feel, for the rest of {p_his} life, like something {p_he} always knew.

choices.text: A dream of flying over the rooftops

effects.log: For years {name} jumps off walls, sure {p_he} can fly. One day, much later, {p_he} nearly can.

choices.text: A dream of a kind stranger

effects.log: {name} grows up trusting strangers a little more than is wise, and is mostly right to.

choices.text: A dream of a warm kitchen

effects.log: Whatever else happens, {name} will always know what home is meant to feel like.

events.text: You reach down and lay a blessing on {name}, the first real touch of heaven {p_he} has ever had. It is a small thing to you and an enormous one to a mortal. You must choose its shape: a blessing is a door, and every door opens one way.

choices.text: The body: strength and good health

effects.log: A fever {name} did not know was coming never comes. The ache in {p_his} back is gone. {name} runs up the hill without stopping, for the first time in years.

choices.text: The mind: clarity at the gate

effects.log: For one season every page {name} reads stays read, and the energy moves the way the manuals promise it should.

choices.text: Fortune: the small luck that changes things

effects.log: A purse found in the road, a door that opens at the right moment, a stranger in a good mood. Nothing anyone could point to.

events.text: {name} is struggling, and you can see exactly where: the knot in the breath, the debt in the drawer, the grief that will not loosen. A blessing cannot fix a life. It can lift one weight for a while, if you choose which.

choices.text: Lift the wounds

effects.log: The old wounds stop hurting in the cold. {name} sleeps through the night and wakes younger.

choices.text: Lift the knot in the breath

effects.log: Something in {name}'s meridians unknots with a feeling like a sigh. The road ahead is shorter by a year.

choices.text: Lift the grief, a little

effects.log: One morning the grief is lighter, not gone. {name} laughs at something for the first time in months.

events.text: {name} is a child, and a blessing on a child is different: it is not help, it is a shape the whole life grows around. You hold it in your hand for a long time before you let it fall.

choices.text: A strong little body

effects.log: {name} is never ill again that whole childhood, and grows tall, and runs everywhere.

choices.text: A quick little mind

effects.log: {name} learns to read in a month and asks a question nobody in the house can answer.

choices.text: A face people trust

effects.log: Strangers smile at {name} in the market. It will open more doors than any sword.

events.text: You decide to send someone into {name}'s life. Not a god: a mortal, already walking somewhere below, whose road you bend a little so it crosses {name}'s. Every life is made of the people in it. You are choosing one.

choices.text: A friend who will stay

effects.log: A stranger shares a table with {name} at a crowded inn, and they talk until the lamps go out. They will be friends for years.

choices.text: Someone to love

effects.log: At a festival, in the crowd by the lantern boats, {name} turns and meets a pair of eyes and forgets what {p_he} was saying.

choices.text: A teacher who sees what {p_he} could be

effects.log: An old wanderer watches {name} train, says "No, like this," and stays a season. {name} learns more in it than in years.

choices.text: A rival to push {p_him} higher

effects.log: Someone {name}'s age wins a contest {name} should have won, and smirks about it. {name} trains twice as hard from that day.

events.text: {name} is lonely in a way that has gone on too long. You look along the roads below for someone walking toward nowhere in particular, someone who could use {name} as much as {name} could use them.

choices.text: A friend with a loud laugh

effects.log: A neighbour moves in next door with a loud laugh and no sense of privacy. {name} is furious, then fond.

choices.text: Someone gentle, to love

effects.log: A traveller with a quiet voice asks {name} the way, and comes back the next day to ask again.

choices.text: An old wanderer with a manual and no heir

effects.log: An old wanderer dies owing {name} a kindness, and pays it back with a battered manual and a season of lessons first.

events.text: {name} is dying. You can see the thread of {p_his} life fraying, strand by strand, and you reach down and take hold of it. Heaven has rules about this. You have broken worse. How will it look, to the mortals below?

choices.text: A fever breaks at dawn

effects.log: The healer had already sent for the family. At dawn the fever breaks like a wave, and {name} asks for water. The healer will tell the story for years.

choices.text: A stranger arrives in time

effects.log: A wandering physician knocks at the right door at the right hour, says nothing, works all night, and is gone by morning.

choices.text: Nobody will ever understand it

effects.log: {name} simply does not die. The wound closes. The breath comes back. Nobody can explain it, least of all {name}.

events.text: A child should not die, and this one is about to. You do not deliberate. Your hand is already reaching before you have decided anything, and the decision, you realise later, was made a whole life ago, when you first looked down.

choices.text: The child wakes, crying for {p_his} supper

effects.log: The house goes from silence to noise in a single breath. {name} is furious to have missed supper. Everyone weeps.

choices.text: A grandmother's remedy works, against all sense

effects.log: An old remedy nobody believed in works, for once. It will be sworn by in that house for three generations.

events.text: {name} is old, but this is not old age: this is a blade, or a fall, or a poison, the murim's kind of ending. You decide it does not get to end like this. Not this one. {name} will die in bed, in time, if you have anything to say about it.

choices.text: Turn the blow aside

effects.log: The death that was coming simply misses. {name} sits in the dust, alive, and laughs like a young fool.

choices.text: Let {p_him} feel your hand, this once

effects.log: For one moment {name} feels a hand on {p_his} back, steadying, and will thank it every night from now on without knowing whose it was.
